sx.profile.credentials.title: Credentials
sx.profile.credentials.desc: How you sign in and how tools sign in as you.
sx.profile.passwordHint: Use at least 12 characters you do not use anywhere else.
sx.profile.tokensHint: Personal tokens for the command line, CI and package clients.
sx.pp.selfCreate.title: Allow users to create projects
sx.pp.selfCreate.hint: When on, any signed-in user can create a project and becomes its owner. Policy fields stay admin-only.
sx.pp.selfCreate.saveFailed: Failed to save the project creation setting
sx.pp.selfCreate.loadFailed: Failed to load the project creation setting
sx.pp.perProject.title: Rules of a project
sx.pp.perProject.hint: Allowed formats, repository types, the name prefix, public repositories, repository limit and token lifetime are set per project, in its settings.
sx.pp.effect.title: What project roles grant
sx.pp.effect.viewer: Viewer: read on every repository the project owns.
sx.pp.effect.developer: Developer: read and write on every repository the project owns.
sx.pp.effect.maintainer: Maintainer and owner: read, write and delete on every repository the project owns. Groups can be attached as viewer, developer or maintainer; owner is personal.
sx.pp.effect.limits: Project roles never grant administration (this API, users, settings) and are added to, never subtract from, permission targets. The built-in system project grants nothing. Tokens limited to specific permission targets do not get project access. Managing projects requires the global admin permission.
sx.quotas.col.name: Name
sx.quotas.summary: {over} over limit, {near} near limit, {ok} within limit.
sx.quotas.summaryAllOk: All {n} quotas are within their limits.
sx.quotas.truncated: Showing the first {shown} of {total} quotas. Narrow the search to see the others.
sx.quotas.emptyHint: A quota stops a repository or project from growing without limit. Set one in the repository configuration, or on the Usage tab of a project.
sx.cleanup.emptyHint: Cleanup policies delete old versions automatically, for example "keep the last 5". Deleted versions go to the trash first, so mistakes are recoverable. Add a policy in the Cleanup section of a hosted repository's Settings tab.
sx.cleanup.partial: Could not read the policies of: {names}.
sx.cleanup.scope: Policies are kept per repository; this list gathers them from every hosted repository. Project default policies are managed on the project.
sx.scanners.summary.none: No scanner is ready. Packages are not scanned for vulnerabilities until one is.
sx.scanners.readyDetail: Installed and its vulnerability data is available.
sx.scanners.activity.title: Scan activity
sx.scanners.configure.title: Configure scanners
sx.scanners.configure.body: Scanners are enabled in the server configuration, not here: set where they keep their databases, how often they refresh, and whether the server may install them. Restart the server after a change.
sx.scanners.loadFailed: Could not load the scanner status.
sx.policies.col.name: Policy
sx.policies.emptyHint: A license policy acts on scan results for every repository: warn about, block or allow packages by their license. Without one, licenses are only reported.
sx.policies.scope: These policies apply to every repository. A repository can add its own on its security tab.
sx.policies.drawer.title: Create policy
sx.policies.field.name: Name
sx.policies.field.actionHint: Block quarantines matching packages. Warn only reports them. Allow marks them as accepted.
sx.policies.field.licensesHint: SPDX identifiers separated by commas or new lines, for example GPL-3.0-only.
sx.policies.nameTooLong: The name is too long (255 characters at most).
sx.policies.editNote: Global policies can be created and listed, but the server does not edit or delete them yet.
sx.fed.off.title: Federation is off for this instance
sx.fed.off.body: Other instances cannot pull from it or push to it, and its repositories do not sync with peers. Turn it on in the server configuration to add peers and issue inbound tokens.
sx.fed.on.title: Federation is on for this instance
sx.fed.on.body: Repositories you federate keep a change log that peer instances pull. Peers are managed per repository.
sx.fed.emptyHint: Open a hosted repository of a supported format, go to its Federation tab and turn federation on, then add a peer.
sx.fed.tokens.title: Inbound tokens
sx.fed.tokens.body: A peer connects to this instance with a token you issue. Create one for each peer and revoke it when the peer is retired.
sx.fed.partial: Could not read the federation status of: {names}.
sx.fed.noRepos: There are no repositories yet, so the server federation state cannot be read.
sx.fed.loadFailed: Could not load the federation overview.
sx.audit.col.subject: Subject
sx.audit.emptyHint: Sign-ins, repository and package changes, token and settings changes are recorded here as they happen.
sx.audit.field.subject: Subject
sx.health.jobs.idle: Nothing queued, no failures in 24 hours
sx.health.jobs.detail: {pending} pending or running, {failed} failed in 24 hours.
sx.health.unscanned.detail: Repositories holding artifacts with no completed scan: {n}
sx.health.unscanned.none: Every repository with artifacts has been scanned
sx.health.build.hint: Include this when you report a problem.
sx.health.unstamped.title: This build was compiled without version metadata (ldflags), so version and commit are not recorded.
sx.health.unstamped.body: Build with make build, or pass the linker flags below, or run an official release image, to see them here and in bug reports.
sx.health.error.title: System status is unavailable
sx.health.error.body: The status endpoints did not answer. Check that the OpenArtifact server is running and that it can reach its database, then try again.
sa.emptyHint: A service account is a named identity for automation. Give it tokens, roles and a trust policy so a CI job can publish without a stored secret.
sa.col.name: Name
sa.disabledToast: Disabled {name}. Its tokens no longer authenticate.
sa.confirmDeleteBody: {name} loses its tokens, group memberships, project roles, role assignments and trust policies. CI jobs that use it stop working. This cannot be undone.
sa.create.title: New service account
sa.create.desc: A non-human identity for automation. It cannot sign in to the web UI.
sa.field.name: Name
sa.field.nameHint: 3 to 64 letters, digits, dashes or underscores. Unique among users and service accounts, and it cannot be changed later.
sa.field.nameInvalid: Use 3 to 64 letters, digits, dashes or underscores.
sa.field.descriptionHint: What the account is for, up to 255 characters.
sa.detail.disabledNote: This account is disabled. Its tokens, including those already issued, authenticate nothing until you enable it again.
sa.detail.policiesDesc: Trust policies that let a CI system exchange its ID token for a short-lived token of this account.
sa.token.title: API tokens
sa.token.desc: Tokens that authenticate as this account. A secret is shown once, when you create it.
sa.token.emptyHint: Create a token for a script that cannot use token exchange. Prefer a trust policy for CI.
sa.token.createTitle: Create a token for this account
sa.token.createDesc: The token authenticates as the service account with the roles shown on this page.
sa.token.kind.access: Access: artifacts and the management API
sa.token.kind.deploy.hint: Can push and pull artifacts but cannot call the management API.
sa.token.kind.access.hint: Can also call the management API with the roles of the account.
sa.token.revealHint: Put it in the secret store of the job that uses this account.
sa.token.revokeDesc: {name} will be revoked. Anything using it, such as CI, stops authenticating immediately. This cannot be undone.
sa.roles.title: Global roles
sa.roles.desc: Permission targets assigned to this account, across the repositories they match.
sa.roles.empty: No permission target is assigned to this account.
sa.roles.noTargets: There is no other permission target to assign.
sa.groups.title: Groups
sa.groups.desc: Groups the account belongs to; it gets what the groups are allowed.
sa.groups.empty: This account is in no group.
sa.projects.title: Project roles
sa.projects.desc: Projects the account is a member of, and its role in each.
sa.projects.empty: This account is a member of no project.
sa.policy.drawerDesc: A CI job whose ID token matches the conditions gets a short-lived token of the service account.
sa.policy.emptyHint: A trust policy lets a CI system, such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, exchange its ID token for a short-lived token without a stored secret.
sa.policy.col.name: Name
sa.policy.confirmDeleteBody: CI jobs can no longer exchange tokens through {name}. Tokens already issued stay valid until they expire; disable the service account to cut them off at once.
sa.preset.label: Start from
sa.policy.name: Name
sa.policy.nameHint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, up to 64. Unique.
sa.policy.issuerHint: The issuer URL exactly as in the iss claim of the ID tokens. It must be https and reachable from this server.
sa.policy.issuerShared: This issuer signs the tokens of every customer, so keep a condition on the repository or project (a pattern that does not start with a wildcard). The server refuses the policy otherwise.
sa.policy.discoveryHint.anonymous: Reads the OpenID configuration and keys of the issuer without credentials.
sa.policy.discoveryHint.static: Verifies tokens against the public keys below and never contacts the issuer; the iss claim must still equal the issuer.
sa.policy.discoveryHint.serviceaccount: Reads the configuration and keys of a Kubernetes API server with this server's own service account token, trusting the cluster CA mounted in its pod.
sa.policy.jwksHint: A JSON Web Key Set with up to 32 public signing keys, for example the output of kubectl get --raw /openid/v1/jwks. Private and symmetric keys are refused.
sa.policy.allowPrivateHint: Allow the issuer and its key URL to resolve to private or cluster-internal addresses. https is still required; link-local and cloud metadata addresses stay blocked.
sa.policy.audienceHint: Must match the audience the CI job requests for its ID token, for example the URL of this server.
sa.policy.accountHint: The identity the exchanged token carries.
sa.policy.problem.name: Use 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores.
sa.policy.problem.audience: Enter the audience the CI job requests.
sa.policy.problem.ttl: Enter a whole number of minutes between 1 and 60.
sa.policy.problem.claim: Every condition needs a claim name, or a dotted path such as kubernetes.io.namespace without empty parts.
sa.policy.problem.jwks: Paste a JSON object: a JWK Set with a keys array.
sa.policy.problem.patterns: Every condition needs at least one pattern.
sa.policy.problem.tooManyPatterns: A condition takes at most 8 patterns.
sa.cond.title: Conditions
sa.cond.hint: Every condition must hold; a condition holds when the claim matches any of its patterns. A claim is a name or a dotted path into nested claims, such as kubernetes.io.namespace. * matches any run of characters, ? one character. Separate patterns with commas or new lines.
sx.recovery.error.title: Could not read the recovery journal
sx.recovery.health.healthy.hint: Every change has its sidecar in storage.
sx.recovery.health.catching-up.hint: Changed rows are waiting for their sidecar. The oldest wait is the recovery point of a rebuild right now.
sx.recovery.health.failing.hint: Some sidecar writes failed and are retried with backoff. Check the last error and the storage backend.
sx.recovery.off.title: The recovery journal is off
sx.recovery.off.body: No sidecars are written, so a rebuild from storage would miss every change made since the journal stopped. Switching it on again queues a full resync.
sx.recovery.lastError.hint: The row is retried with backoff (5 seconds up to 15 minutes); the error stays until the next success replaces it.
sx.recovery.rebuild.body: If the database is lost and no backup is usable, the sidecars let an empty database get its package index back from the blob store. Stop every server first, point the configuration at an empty database, then run:
sx.recovery.rebuild.note: A rebuild runs on the command line, not from this page, and the server keeps no history of it. Users, permissions, tokens, audit logs and settings are not in the sidecars.
sx.attestation.off.title: Attestations are not enabled
sx.attestation.off.body: This server does not sign SBOM and VEX documents. Enable attestations in the server configuration to get a signing key.
sx.attestation.secret-required.title: A secret key is needed
sx.attestation.secret-required.body: The signing key is only stored encrypted, so the server cannot generate one without OPENARTIFACT_SECRET_KEY. Set it, or point attestation.keyPath at a key file.
sx.attestation.error.title: Could not read the signing key
sx.attestation.key.hint: Signs the SBOM and VEX attestations. Keep the public key of every key that ever signed one: older attestations verify only against the key that signed them.
sx.attestation.keyId: Key ID (sha256 of the public key)
sx.attestation.source.generated: Generated by the server, stored encrypted
sx.attestation.verify.hint: Downloads the public key and checks a signed SBOM bundle offline with cosign. Add ?attest=bundle to an SBOM download to get the bundle.
sx.attestation.attach.hint: A hosted docker repository can sign the SBOM and VEX of an image and attach them to it as OCI referrers, where cosign and oras find them.
sx.attestation.attach.emptyHint: Attestations are attached only to images of hosted docker repositories.
sx.attestation.attach.error: Could not list the docker repositories.
sx.declarative.intro: Manage configuration as YAML manifests, as oa apply does: review exactly what would change, then apply it. Every change is made with your own permissions and is audited as yours.
sx.declarative.manifest.hint: Paste YAML or load files. Several documents are separated by a line with three dashes.
sx.declarative.placeholder:
apiVersion: openartifact.io/v1
kind: Group
metadata:
  name: platform
spec:
  description: Platform team
sx.declarative.kinds.hint: Limit the review and the apply to these kinds. Nothing selected means all of them (and Users are exported only when selected).
sx.declarative.prune: Delete what the manifest no longer lists
sx.declarative.prune.hint: Removes the objects apply created or adopted earlier that are missing from this manifest.
sx.declarative.pruneAll: Delete everything not listed, managed or not
sx.declarative.pruneAll.hint: Removes every object of the selected kinds that the manifest omits, except built-in ones. Review the list carefully.
sx.declarative.forceSecrets: Send secrets even when already set
sx.declarative.forceSecrets.hint: Normally a secret the server reports as set is left alone.
sx.declarative.continue.hint: Apply the remaining items when one fails, instead of skipping them.
sx.declarative.reviewFirst: Review the changes before applying them.
sx.declarative.invalid: The manifest is not valid. Nothing was read from the server.
sx.declarative.unapplicable: These problems stop the plan from being applied:
sx.declarative.noChanges: The server already matches the manifest. There is nothing to apply.
sx.declarative.deleteUnmanaged: not managed, removed by delete everything
sx.declarative.adopt: existing object, will be recorded as managed
sx.declarative.secrets.hint: The manifest refers to secrets by environment variable name. Enter their values here: they are sent once with the request and never stored or shown again.
sx.declarative.secrets.provided: A value was sent with this review.
sx.declarative.secrets.file: The manifest reads a secret from the file {path}. The server never reads files for a manifest: use an environment reference.
sx.declarative.confirm.title: Apply these changes?
sx.declarative.confirm.body: The server is changed as shown in the plan. Review it again if anything has changed since.
sx.declarative.confirm.withDeletes: This deletes the objects listed below, as well as making the other changes in the plan.
sx.declarative.applied.failed: Some changes failed. See the result.
sx.declarative.managed.hint: Objects created or adopted by apply. Only these are deleted when you delete what a manifest no longer lists.
sx.declarative.managed.emptyHint: Objects appear here once you apply a manifest.
sx.declarative.col.name: Name
sx.declarative.release.title: Stop managing this object?
sx.declarative.release.body: {name} stays as it is. Apply will no longer delete it when a manifest omits it.
sx.gate.intro: Findings carry exploitation signals: whether a vulnerability is in the CISA KEV catalog and how likely FIRST EPSS rates its exploitation. A gate fails a scan when any condition below holds. Checking a scan only reports; blocking downloads means quarantining it.
sx.gate.criteria.hint: A scan fails when any one condition holds for any of its findings, the same rule a CI job applies.
sx.gate.kev.hint: A finding is in the CISA KEV catalog.
sx.gate.epss.hint: A finding is rated at least this likely to be exploited.
sx.gate.epss.hintThreshold: A finding rated at least this likely to be exploited. Findings reach the epss priority from {threshold}.
sx.gate.epss.invalid: Enter a percentage above 0 and up to 100.
sx.gate.noCriteria: Choose at least one condition to see which scans meet it.
sx.gate.matching.hint: Open scans with a finding that meets a condition, most urgent first.
sx.gate.matching.empty: No open scan meets the gate
sx.gate.matching.emptyHint: Nothing to block for these conditions.
sx.gate.truncated: More scans meet the gate than are listed. The most urgent are shown.
sx.gate.block.title: Block downloads of this scan?
sx.gate.block.body: {name} is quarantined: downloads are refused with 403 and it cannot be promoted until you release it.
sx.gate.blockedTitle.hint: Scans in quarantine. Their downloads are refused and promotion is refused.
sx.gate.release.title: Release this scan?
sx.gate.release.body: Downloads and promotion of {name} are allowed again.
sx.gate.feedsOff.title: Exploitation data is off
sx.gate.feedsOff.body: Without the KEV and EPSS feeds, findings carry no exploitation signals and a gate has nothing to match. Blocked scans are still listed below.
sx.vexFeeds.intro: A vendor CSAF provider publishes which of its products are not affected by a vulnerability or have it fixed. Each sync reads the documents changed since the last one, checks their hashes and OpenPGP signatures, and records the matching statements as VEX decisions of the scanned packages. A decision recorded by an administrator is never replaced.
sx.vexFeeds.emptyHint: Add the provider-metadata.json of a vendor that publishes CSAF advisories for the packages you host.
sx.vexFeeds.loadFailed: Failed to load the VEX feeds
sx.vexFeeds.syncRunning: A sync of {name} is already running
sx.vexFeeds.deleteBody: The decisions it recorded are removed with it; findings they marked not affected show up again.
sx.vexFeeds.deleteFailed: Failed to delete the VEX feed
sx.vexFeeds.saveFailed: Failed to save the VEX feed
sx.vexFeeds.field.name: Name
sx.vexFeeds.field.nameHint: Letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', up to 63 characters.
sx.vexFeeds.field.urlHint: A CSAF provider-metadata.json, a ROLIE feed or a single CSAF document, over https.
sx.vexFeeds.field.keysHint: ASCII-armored public keys that sign the documents. When empty, the keys listed in the provider metadata are used.
sx.vexFeeds.field.requireSignatureHint: Documents without a valid OpenPGP signature are rejected.
sx.vexFeeds.field.enabledHint: Sync the feed on its interval.
sx.vexFeeds.error.name.invalid: Use letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit (63 characters at most).
sx.vexFeeds.error.pgpKeys.tooLarge: The keys are limited to 64 KiB.
sx.vexFeeds.error.intervalHours.range: Enter a whole number of hours between {min} and {max}.
